items.title: Man jailed after threatening to behead son’s teacher in French village
items.description: A man has been given a six-month jail term in France after he threatened to behead a female primary school teacher who had disciplined his son at a village primary school. The 47-year-old was sentenced after a fast-track hearing on Thursday, six days after the events unfolded in Le Fauga, a village with a population of about 2,600 just outside the southwestern city of Toulouse. The teacher has been granted official protection and has gone on sick leave. French Education Minister Edouard Geffray said: “No teacher should be afraid to do their job. Attacking one of them is attacking the entire institution.” Over the summer, Geffray steered through a law aimed at protecting staff from a “significant risk” to their safety or health from a member of a student’s family. The minister said this case would trigger one of the first uses of the decree. The case revives terrible memories in France of the beheading of a teacher in the Paris suburb of Conflans-Sainte-Honorine six years ago. Samuel Paty was murdered in a jihadist attack outside his school by an 18-year-old Chechen refugee. In Le Fauga, the teacher’s colleagues did not go into work on Monday because of what had happened the previous Friday. The threat was made after the man had been called in for a chat with the school, according to Toulouse education chief Karim Benmiloud. Le Fauga Mayor Jean-Marie Puig told BFMTV that the man’s son had been disruptive in class and he had been sent to another class to calm down. The child continued to misbehave in the second classroom and the teacher later told him off for acting up. The teacher was later threatened by the father, who according to the mayor had waited for her “outside the school and apparently threatened to cut off her head if she’d been a man”. The parent subsequently apologised, however a judicial complaint was made and he went before a judge in Toulouse on Thursday afternoon. According to French reports from the court in Toulouse, the judge told the man that such remarks were disturbing, particularly in light of the Samuel Paty case, “which remains fresh in the minds of all French people”. The Toulouse prosecutor had asked for a period of six months’ house arrest, however the judge said the man should serve the time in jail because of the seriousness of his actions. “I’m really not proud of myself,” the man said, according to the prosecutor’s team. The sentence also requires him to undergo a citizenship course and avoid contacting the victim or approaching the school. The decree passed in July allows for a student to be transferred to another school in a case involving significant risk to staff, and where education authorities have intervened. It is thought the boy and a younger sister may now be moved to another school outside Le Fauga. The teacher involved, who is in her 50s, is said to be very shocked by the threat.

items.title: Reboisement du massif anacardier : la Casamance replante son « or blanc »
items.description: Le CROFAZ a lancé hier, une campagne de reboisement pour régénérer le massif anacardier et redonner du souffle à une filière qui fait vivre de nombreuses familles dans le Sud du pays. Avec 80 000 plants déjà mis en place cette année, l’ambition est d’améliorer les rendements, créer des emplois et renforcer l’autonomie de production. À Djibonker, de jeunes plants portent déjà les espoirs d’une filière qui nourrit des milliers de familles en Casamance. Le Cadre régional de concertation des opérateurs de la filière anacarde de Ziguinchor (CROFAZ) y a lancé hier une campagne de reboisement destinée à régénérer le massif anacardier et à améliorer durablement la productivité des vergers. « Cette année, nous avons déjà mis en place 80 000 plants. Dans cinq ans, nous visons l’autonomie de production et une couverture de 99 % des besoins nationaux », annonce le président du CROFAZ, Demba Diémé. Pour atteindre cet objectif, l’organisation mise sur la formation de relais agricoles et la diversification des exploitations avec le maïs, l’arachide et l’apiculture. Une stratégie qui doit permettre aux producteurs de mieux valoriser leurs terres tout en sécurisant leurs revenus. Car, malgré son poids économique, la filière reste confrontée à de faibles rendements, estimés entre 300 et 400 kg à l’hectare au Sénégal. Plantations trop serrées, techniques culturales insuffisantes, divagation des animaux et manque d’encadrement continuent de freiner son potentiel. « Sans une production solide, la transformation restera un vœu pieux », avertit Demba Diémé. À Djibonker, dans le département de Ziguinchor, les producteurs commencent à mesurer l’intérêt des nouvelles pratiques. « Avec une bonne distanciation, nous pouvons cultiver d’autres spéculations entre les anacardiers. C’est une véritable révolution pour nous », témoigne Rigobert Sagna. Même enthousiasme chez Léonie Biagui, adjointe au chef du village. « Nous avons découvert une réelle différence entre nos anciennes pratiques et les nouvelles méthodes. Elles permettent aux fruits de mieux grossir et rendent l’exploitation plus productive », magnifie-t-elle. Pour Marc Lopy, président de la jeunesse de Djibonker, l’enjeu est également social. « La terre ne ment jamais. Cette campagne de reboisement est une chance pour Djibonker et pour toute la Casamance. L’agriculture peut offrir aux jeunes des revenus et des perspectives », soutient-il. Mais la réussite de cette ambition dépendra aussi de l’accompagnement des producteurs, des infrastructures de collecte et de transformation et d’un meilleur encadrement de la filière. À Djibonker, le CROFAZ entend ainsi planter bien plus que des anacardiers. Cette structure que dirige Demba Diémé compte y semer les graines d’une filière plus productive, plus créatrice d’emplois et capable de consolider une activité essentielle à l’économie familiale en Casamance. Gaustin DIATTA (Correspondant)

items.title: Mahama commends Nadowli 24-Hour Market contractor
items.description: President John Mahama has commended the contractor working on the 24-hour market project at Nadowli in the Nadowli-Kaleo District of the Upper West Region. Inspecting the project, President Mahama said the contractor was making good progress and has demonstrated the capacity to commence work. “Let me commend the contractor who is working on this project.” President Mahama said the government is constructing 24-hour markets in all 261 constituencies, stressing that contractors awarded the projects are expected to have the financial capacity to begin work with their own resources. “We are constructing these 24-Hour Markets in all 261 constituencies, and I can see that this is a serious contractor,” he said. He explained that contractors were not expected to wait for mobilisation before commencing work, recalling instances in the past where mobilisation funds were allegedly misused. “Some contractors assume they will first receive mobilisation, just as happened in the past, when people took mobilisation money and bought V8 vehicles instead of doing the job,” he said. According to President Mahama, companies awarded the contracts were expected to finance the initial stages of the projects from their own resources. “We therefore expected that companies awarded these projects would have the financial muscle to start work with their own resources,” he said. He explained that once a contractor reaches 15 per cent completion, payment would be made to allow the work to continue until completion. “Once a contractor reaches 15 per cent completion, payment is made, and the work continues until the project is finished,” President Mahama said. He added, “The money is available, so there is no reason why any contractor should fail to advance the work to this stage.” President Mahama further commended the contractor at Nadowli, saying the project was on track. “From what I have seen here, the contractor is on track and is doing a very good job. I encourage you to continue the good work,” he said. The President said the 261 markets would contribute to the economic development of communities by providing farmers with reliable outlets for their produce. “These markets are going to strengthen the economic life of our communities,” he said. He noted that farmers producing pepper, onions, maize and other crops would have spaces to display their goods and earn decent incomes. “These 261 markets across the country will provide trading spaces for our pepper farmers, onion farmers, maize farmers, and many others,” President Mahama said. “They will have a place to display their goods and earn a decent income.” He therefore urged other contractors working on similar projects to emulate the progress being made at Nadowli. “That is why these markets are so important, and I hope all the other contractors working on similar projects will take a cue from what is happening here in Nadowli,” he said. He assured residents that upon completion, he would return to commission the facility with the chiefs and the people. “Continue the work, and when you finish, we will all return here, invite the chiefs, and commission the market together,” President Mahama said.

Zio : La Cour constitutionnelle présente sa mission aux acteurs socio-économiques de la Maritime
items.description: Tsévié, 11 sept. (ATOP) – Les membres de la Cour constitutionnelle ont échangé, le vendredi 11 septembre à Tsévié, avec les représentants des différents groupes socio-économiques de la région Maritime sur les attributions de l’institution. Les différents groupes socio-économiques Cette rencontre s’inscrit dans le cadre de la deuxième édition des « Entretiens de la Cour constitutionnelle », un programme destiné à rapprocher l’institution des citoyens et à leur permettre de mieux comprendre son fonctionnement et ses missions. Les échanges ont notamment porté sur la place de la Cour constitutionnelle dans la consolidation de l’Etat de droit et de la démocratie. Ils ont également permis d’expliquer aux participants les différents moyens dont disposent les citoyens pour saisir la Cour afin de faire valoir leurs droits et libertés garantis par la Constitution. Le président de la Cour constitutionnelle, Prof. Djobo-Babakane Coulibaley, a rappelé que l’institution est chargée de veiller au respect de la loi fondamentale et de statuer sur la constitutionnalité des lois et de certains règlements intérieurs des institutions. Il a ajouté que la Cour garantit également les droits fondamentaux de la personne humaine et les libertés publiques. Ses décisions sont définitives et ne sont pas susceptibles de recours. Le gouverneur de la région Maritime, Taïrou Bagbiegue, a relevé que la Cour constitutionnelle est souvent perçue uniquement comme une institution intervenant dans les questions électorales. Il a souhaité que ces échanges contribuent à mieux faire connaître ses missions, ses attributions et son rôle dans la protection des droits et libertés. ATOP/BBG/AO
